title: 第三十三章第三十四章第三十五章
slug: 纳玄尘第五十三章安凌
content_zh:
地宫的正式入口，最后选在了马场和朔州东门之间的路边。
半年前老周找到这个位置的时候，这里只有一间歪歪斜斜的破屋——门窗不全，屋顶塌了一角，野草从墙根长到窗台高。他掀开地板看了一眼下面的空间，抬头对苏尘说了一句：“位置正好。地下的通道挖到这儿了，差最后一截没接上。“
苏尘当时站在门口，回头看了一眼——五里外的马场隐约看得见围墙，再远一点是朔州城门的轮廓。这条路偶尔有过往的车马，不多不少，正好够一个路边小店活下去。
“就这儿。“他说。
半年后，破屋变成了一间不大的客栈。临街的门脸翻新过了，暗红色的门板，门楣上挂着一块新做的木匾，写了三个字——歇脚堂。窗台上搁了两盆不知道是谁种的草，绿油油的，看着像那么回事。屋里摆了三张旧木桌，几条长凳，柜台上搁着一只粗陶茶壶和几只倒扣的碗。看着不起眼，但该有的都有了。
苏尘站在柜台边上，把最后一摞碗码进柜子下层。老周蹲在门口调整门闩的松紧，阿离坐在靠窗的位置，手里端着一碗凉茶，慢慢喝着。陶夭夭蹲在灶台那边，把新买的盐罐和油瓶归进壁龛里。
“行了。“苏尘拍了拍手上的灰，从柜台后面走出来，“差不多了。“
老周站起来，试了试门闩的松紧，点了点头。
“里头呢？“陶夭夭从灶台边探出头。
苏尘没有回答，偏过头看了老周一眼。老周把门关上，从里面插好门闩，然后转身，朝后院的方向抬了抬下巴。
“跟我来。“
后院不大，一棵半枯的老槐树占了半个院子，树下堆着几捆干柴。老周走到正对后门的那间屋子门口——这间屋子的门比其他屋子都厚实一些，门上的铁环擦得发亮。
他推开门。
屋里不大，一张旧书案摆在正中央，案上搁着一盏油灯和一方砚台。靠墙放着一只半旧的木柜，柜门关着。窗纸是新糊的，透进来的光线把整间屋子照得柔和。
看起来就是一间普通的账房。
老周走到书案前，蹲下来，伸手在书案底部摸了一下。他摸到什么东西，按下去——咔的一声轻响。
书案缓缓往后平移了三尺，露出底下一个方方正正的洞口。
洞口下面是一级一级往下延伸的石阶，石阶两侧的墙壁上每隔几步嵌着一盏油灯，火光沿着阶梯一路往下蔓延，消失在深处的拐角处。
老周没有回头看他们。他第一个走下台阶，脚步声在通道里响了一下，然后被石壁吸走了。
苏尘跟在他后面走下去。陶夭夭站在洞口边上看了一眼，然后也跟了下去。阿离走在最后，她下去之前顺手把屋门带上了——门合上的瞬间，咔嗒一声，外面的光线被切断，只剩下通道里油灯的光。

石阶不长。大约走了二十来级，到底之后是一条通道，通道不宽，两个人并排走就有点挤。但走了几步之后，空间忽然开阔起来——通道开始分出岔路，一条向左，一条向右，中间还有一条继续往前。岔路之间是墙壁和转角，再往前走几步，又出现一个新的岔口。
老周在第一个岔口前停下来，侧过身，让出半个身位。
“往这走。“他说，声音不高，但在石壁间回荡了一下才散开。“客栈下来这一整片都是。岔路多，空室也多，多数岔路是死路，不认路的人进来转上半个时辰也走不出去。空室暂时空着，以后也可以堆东西、住人。“
他没有停下来细讲，说完就继续往前走。他走这条路走得极熟——在岔口前从不犹豫，遇转弯提前半步就偏过身体，像是在走一条只有他看得见标记的路。
苏尘跟在他后面，步伐不快不慢。阿离沉默地跟在苏尘身后，陶夭夭在最后——她一边走一边留意老周转弯的方向和岔口的特征，但走了几个岔口之后她发现自己已经开始记混了。
大约走了一盏茶的工夫，通道忽然变得开阔起来。
一个岔口在面前展开——不是普通的岔路，是一个宽敞的空间，四壁规整，顶上嵌了几块打磨过的晶石，把油灯的光折射成柔和的光晕。四条通道从这个空间延伸出去，分别朝向四个不同的方向——来路一条，左右各一条，正前方一条。
十字路口。
老周在中央站定，转过身来。
“这里的十字路口。“他说，“后边——就是咱们来的方向，通客栈。右手边这条道通的就是咱们平常去的马场地下的那个大厅。左手边则是少主要求的地方。前方的话···“
他顿了一下。
“少主不如先去左边看看。“
content_en:
The official entrance to the underground palace was finally chosen on the roadside between the racecourse and the east gate of Shuozhou.
When Lao Zhou found this location half a year ago, there was only a crooked and dilapidated house - with incomplete doors and windows, a corner of the roof collapsed, and weeds growing from the base of the wall to the height of the window sill. He lifted up the floor and took a look at the space below. He raised his head and said to Su Chen: "The location is just right. The underground passage has been dug up to here, but the last section has not been connected."
Su Chen was standing at the door and glanced back - he could vaguely see the wall of the racecourse five miles away, and further away was the outline of Shuozhou City Gate. Occasionally there are cars and horses passing by on this road, no more and no less, just enough for a roadside shop to survive.
"Right here," he said.
Half a year later, the dilapidated house became a small inn. The door facing the street has been renovated, with a dark red door panel and a newly made wooden plaque hanging on the lintel with three words written on it - resting hall. There were two pots of grass planted by someone on the windowsill. They were green and looked like that. There were three old wooden tables and several benches in the room. There was a stoneware teapot and several upside-down bowls placed on the counter. It looks inconspicuous, but it has everything it needs.
Su Chen stood at the edge of the counter and put the last pile of bowls into the lower shelf of the cabinet. Lao Zhou squatted at the door to adjust the tightness of the door latch. A Li sat by the window, holding a bowl of herbal tea in his hand and drinking it slowly. Tao Yaoyao squatted on the stove and put the newly bought salt shaker and oil bottle into the alcove.
"Okay." Su Chen patted the dust on his hands and walked out from behind the counter, "It's almost done."
Lao Zhou stood up, tried the tightness of the door latch, and nodded.
"Where's it inside?" Tao Yaoyao poked her head out from the stove.
Su Chen didn't answer, but turned his head and glanced at Lao Zhou. Lao Zhou closed the door, inserted the latch from the inside, then turned around and raised his chin towards the backyard.
"Follow me."
The backyard is not big. A half-withered old locust tree occupies half of the yard. There are several bundles of dry firewood piled under the tree. Lao Zhou walked to the door of the room directly opposite the back door - the door of this room was thicker than the other rooms, and the iron ring on the door was polished to a shine.
He pushed open the door.
The room was not big. An old book table was placed in the center, with an oil lamp and an inkstone placed on it. There was an old wooden cabinet against the wall, with the door closed. The window paper was newly papered, and the light coming in softly illuminated the whole room.
It looks like an ordinary accounting room.
Lao Zhou walked to the desk, squatted down, and touched the bottom of the desk. He touched something and pressed it - there was a soft click.
The book desk slowly moved back three feet, revealing a square hole underneath.
Below the entrance of the cave are stone steps extending downward one by one. On the walls on both sides of the stone steps are oil lamps embedded every few steps. The fire spreads all the way down the steps and disappears in the deep corners.
Lao Zhou didn't look back at them. He was the first to go down the steps, his footsteps echoed in the passage, and then he was sucked away by the stone wall.
Su Chen walked down behind him. Tao Yaoyao stood at the entrance of the cave and took a look, then followed. A Li walked at the end, and she closed the door behind her before going down. The moment the door closed, there was a click, and the light outside was cut off, leaving only the light of the oil lamp in the passage.
The stone steps are not long. After walking about twenty steps, there is a passage at the end. The passage is not wide, so it would be a bit crowded for two people walking side by side. But after walking a few steps, the space suddenly opened up - the passage began to fork, one to the left, one to the right, and another in the middle that continued forward. Between the forks is a wall and a corner. A few steps further, a new fork appears.
Lao Zhou stopped at the first fork, turned sideways, and gave up half of his body.
"Go this way." He said, his voice was not loud, but it echoed among the stone walls for a while before he dispersed. "This whole area is just down from the inn. There are many forked roads and empty rooms. Most of the forked roads are dead ends, and people who don't know the way come in.I couldn't get out even after half an hour. The empty room is temporarily empty, and can be used to store things and live in people in the future. "
He didn't stop to elaborate and just kept walking. He was very familiar with walking this road - he never hesitated before a fork in the road, and when he encountered a turn, he turned half a step ahead, as if he was walking on a path only he could see the markings.
Su Chen followed him, neither fast nor slow. A Li followed Su Chen silently, with Tao Yaoyao at the end. As she walked, she paid attention to the direction Lao Zhou turned and the features of the forks, but after walking a few forks, she found that she had begun to forget.
After walking for about a cup of tea, the passage suddenly became wider.
A fork opened in front of you - not an ordinary fork, but a spacious space with regular walls and a few polished crystals embedded on the top, which refracted the light of the oil lamp into a soft halo. Four passages extend from this space, heading in four different directions - one from the way forward, one to the left and one to the left, and one directly ahead.
crossroads.
Lao Zhou stood still in the center and turned around.
“The crossroads here. "He said, "The back - is the direction we came from, leading to the inn. The passage on the right leads to the hall underneath the racecourse where we usually go. On the left is the place requested by the young master. Words ahead..."
He paused.
"Young Master, why don't you go to the left and take a look first. "
